## Objetivo

Ajustar un modelo de **regresión lineal múltiple** por **Mínimos Cuadrados Ordinarios (OLS)** y comprobar las hipótesis básicas del modelo
(misma lógica que en el post del profesor: estimación → diagnóstico → posibles correcciones). 

Trabajaremos con el dataset **longley** (incluido en R), que se usa como ejemplo por su **alta colinealidad**.

## Preparación


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
data(longley)

library(lmtest)
library(nortest)
library(car)
```
:::


1) Estimación del modelo (OLS)

En el ejemplo del profesor se ajusta:

Employed = \beta_0 + \beta_1 \cdot GNP.deflator + \beta_2 \cdot GNP + \beta_3 \cdot Population + u


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
reg <- lm(Employed ~ GNP.deflator + GNP + Population, data = longley)
summary(reg)
```

## 2) Diagnóstico de hipótesis básicas

### 2.1 Multicolinealidad

En el temario se proponen 3 vías:

- determinante de la matriz de correlaciones (cerca de 0 ⇒ relación lineal alta)

- VIF (valores > 10 preocupante)

- Número de condición (valores > 30 preocupante)


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
X <- longley[, c("GNP.deflator", "GNP", "Population")]

det(cor(X))        # determinante de la matriz de correlaciones
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 0.0002842754
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
vif(reg)           # VIF
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
GNP.deflator          GNP   Population 
    62.40594    145.06696     58.92490 
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
kappa(model.matrix(reg))  # número de condición (aprox.)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 44124.11
```


:::
:::


### 2.2 Heterocedasticidad

En este caso:

- métodos gráficos con residuos y residuos^2

- tests analíticos (White, Breusch–Pagan, Goldfeld–Quandt) con lmtest


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
e <- reg$residuals
e2 <- e^2

plot(e, type = "b", main = "Residuos por observación", ylab = "e", xlab = "i")
abline(h = 0, lwd = 2)
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](index_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-4-1.png){width=672}
:::

```{.r .cell-code}
plot(reg$fitted.values, e, main = "Residuos vs Ajustados", xlab = "ŷ", ylab = "e")
abline(h = 0, lwd = 2)
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](index_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-4-2.png){width=672}
:::
:::



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
decision <- function(p, alpha = 0.05, h0 = "H0") {
  if (is.na(p)) return("p-value NA")
  if (p < alpha) paste("Rechazo", h0, "(p <", alpha, ")")
  else paste("No rechazo", h0, "(p ≥", alpha, ")")
}
```
:::


Breusch–Pagan y Goldfeld–Quandt (lmtest):

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
bp <- bptest(reg)
gq <- gqtest(reg, fraction = 1/3, order.by = longley$GNP)

bp
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

	studentized Breusch-Pagan test

data:  reg
BP = 4.2476, df = 3, p-value = 0.2359
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
cat(decision(bp$p.value, h0 = "homocedasticidad"), "\n")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
No rechazo homocedasticidad (p ≥ 0.05 ) 
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
gq
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

	Goldfeld-Quandt test

data:  reg
GQ = 2042.6, df1 = 2, df2 = 1, p-value = 0.01564
alternative hypothesis: variance increases from segment 1 to 2
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
cat(decision(gq$p.value, h0 = "homocedasticidad"), "\n")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
Rechazo homocedasticidad (p < 0.05 ) 
```


:::
:::


White

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Construcción de términos (cuadrados e interacciones)
GNP.deflator <- longley$GNP.deflator
GNP <- longley$GNP
Population <- longley$Population

aux <- lm(e2 ~ GNP.deflator + GNP + Population +
            I(GNP.deflator^2) + I(GNP^2) + I(Population^2) +
            I(GNP.deflator*GNP) + I(GNP.deflator*Population) + I(GNP*Population))

R2_aux <- summary(aux)[[8]]
n <- nrow(longley)

stat <- n * R2_aux
df <- summary(aux)[[10]][[2]]   # g.l. numerador en el aux (como en el PDF)
crit <- qchisq(0.95, df)
p_white <- pchisq(stat, df = df, lower.tail = FALSE)
c(stat = stat, df = df, p_value = p_white)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
     stat        df   p_value 
5.6267158 9.0000000 0.7766183 
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
cat(decision(p_white, h0 = "homocedasticidad (White)"), "\n")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
No rechazo homocedasticidad (White) (p ≥ 0.05 ) 
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
c(stat = stat, crit = crit)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
     stat      crit 
 5.626716 16.918978 
```


:::
:::


### 2.3 Autocorrelación

En el temario se detecta:

- gráfico de residuos por orden

- gráfico residuos vs retardo (lag)

- contraste Durbin–Watson (dwtest).


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# lag 1 de residuos
e_lag <- e[-length(e)]
e_now <- e[-1]

plot(e_now, e_lag, main = "Residuos vs retardo (lag 1)", xlab = "e_t", ylab = "e_{t-1}")
abline(lm(e_lag ~ e_now), lwd = 2)
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](index_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-8-1.png){width=672}
:::

```{.r .cell-code}
dwtest(reg)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

	Durbin-Watson test

data:  reg
DW = 1.1698, p-value = 0.008272
alternative hypothesis: true autocorrelation is greater than 0
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
dw <- dwtest(reg)
dw
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

	Durbin-Watson test

data:  reg
DW = 1.1698, p-value = 0.008272
alternative hypothesis: true autocorrelation is greater than 0
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
cat(decision(dw$p.value, h0 = "incorrelación (DW)"), "\n")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
Rechazo incorrelación (DW) (p < 0.05 ) 
```


:::
:::


### 2.4 Normalidad de residuos

En el temario se aplican Kolmogorov–Smirnov, Shapiro–Wilk y Lilliefors.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ks.test(e, pnorm, mean(e), sd(e))
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

	Exact one-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test

data:  e
D = 0.098933, p-value = 0.993
alternative hypothesis: two-sided
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
shapiro.test(e)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

	Shapiro-Wilk normality test

data:  e
W = 0.97743, p-value = 0.9399
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
lillie.test(e)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

	Lilliefors (Kolmogorov-Smirnov) normality test

data:  e
D = 0.098933, p-value = 0.9446
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
ks <- ks.test(e, pnorm, mean(e), sd(e))
sw <- shapiro.test(e)
lf <- lillie.test(e)

ks; cat(decision(ks$p.value, h0="normalidad (KS)"), "\n")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

	Exact one-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test

data:  e
D = 0.098933, p-value = 0.993
alternative hypothesis: two-sided
```


:::

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
No rechazo normalidad (KS) (p ≥ 0.05 ) 
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
sw; cat(decision(sw$p.value, h0="normalidad (Shapiro)"), "\n")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

	Shapiro-Wilk normality test

data:  e
W = 0.97743, p-value = 0.9399
```


:::

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
No rechazo normalidad (Shapiro) (p ≥ 0.05 ) 
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
lf; cat(decision(lf$p.value, h0="normalidad (Lilliefors)"), "\n")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

	Lilliefors (Kolmogorov-Smirnov) normality test

data:  e
D = 0.098933, p-value = 0.9446
```


:::

No rechazo normalidad (Lilliefors) (p ≥ 0.05 )

## 3) Correcciones (opcional / “por si sale mal”)

### 3.1 Corrección de heterocedasticidad (WLS)

Si se conoce un patrón de varianza, el profesor muestra el uso de weights= en lm.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
reg_wls <- lm(Employed ~ GNP.deflator + GNP + Population, data = longley, weights = GNP)
summary(reg_wls)
```
:::


### 3.2 Corrección de autocorrelación (Prais–Winsten / Cochrane–Orcutt)

El temario enseña ambas.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# install.packages(c("prais", "orcutt"))
library(prais)
library(orcutt)

reg_pw <- prais_winsten(Employed ~ GNP.deflator + GNP + Population,
                        data = longley, index = 1:nrow(longley))
summary(reg_pw)

reg_co <- cochrane.orcutt(reg)
summary(reg_co)
```
:::



## Conclusiones

1. Ajustamos el modelo OLS con lm() y leímos summary() como en los ejemplos. 

2. Revisamos hipótesis: multicolinealidad (det/VIF/condición), heterocedasticidad (BP/GQ/White), autocorrelación (DW), normalidad (KS/Shapiro/Lilliefors).

3. Si hay incumplimientos, dejamos preparadas correcciones típicas (WLS y ajustes por autocorrelación).
